summary: ING sits clearly with the traditional banks (position score 0.21) and its measured signature is verbal rather than interactive: it quotes far more figures than peers (25.5 versus a peer mean of 12.15) and is fully mobile-first, but it carries far fewer calls to action (2.0 versus 13.38) and no comparison table. Every one of these is a design observation with no performance data behind it, so each recommendation is a hypothesis to test rather than a cause. The search context adds that ING held 18.13% of Belgian brand search attention at rank 3, down 2.49 points across Sep 2021–Sep 2026.

recommendations.title: Restore calls to action on the current-account pages
recommendations.finding: ING shows 2.0 calls to action per page against a peer mean of 13.38, about 1.06 standard deviations below peers and the clearest structural deficit in the comparison.
recommendations.recommendation: Add explicit, repeated calls to action down the current-account pages (open an account, book an appointment, compare packs) so that every scroll depth offers a next step.

recommendations.title: Audit the volume of figures quoted
recommendations.finding: ING quotes 25.5 figures or percentages per page against a peer mean of 12.15, more than 1.4 standard deviations above the market and the strongest single element of ING's signature.
recommendations.recommendation: Review every number on the page and keep only those with a dated, verifiable source; move the rest into a short footnote or drop them, so that the density of figures does not outrun the evidence behind them.

recommendations.title: Shorten the page and give it a clearer spine
recommendations.finding: ING's pages run 9,465 px against a peer mean of 6,414 px, 0.91 standard deviations above peers, while carrying the fewest calls to action in the set: a long page with few exits.
recommendations.recommendation: Cut or collapse the lower sections of the current-account page and tie each remaining section to one message and one action, then test the shorter version against the current one.

recommendations.title: Add a comparison table to the pack pages
recommendations.finding: No ING page in the set includes a comparison table, against a peer mean of 0.38, a common market element that is absent from ING's pages.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a simple pack comparison table (monthly fee, card, app features, conditions) on the current-account pages, using only figures ING can substantiate.

recommendations.title: Give students and young people a dedicated entry point
recommendations.finding: ING targets students or young people (1.0 versus a peer mean of 0.38, roughly 1.2 standard deviations above peers), one of its clearest signature signals, but on a limited number of pages.
recommendations.recommendation: Route the youth offer to a dedicated young-customer page rather than a block on the main pack page: one offer, one eligibility line, one call to action, linked from the current-account page.

recommendations.title: Complete the AIDA sequence instead of the desire stage alone
recommendations.finding: ING's campaign structure is more complete than peers (3.5 versus 2.71) and it scores fully on making the offer feel worth having (1.0 versus 0.43), yet it carries the fewest calls to action, so the sequence is heavy on desire and light on action.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the desire section but close the sequence with an explicit action block, and check that attention, interest, desire and action each appear once and in order rather than as repeated desire blocks.

recommendations.title: Extend the mobile-first treatment across the whole journey
recommendations.finding: ING is fully mobile-first (1.0) against a peer mean of 0.38, and in this set challengers score 1.0 on mobile-first design against 0.29 for traditional banks, so this is a strength rather than a deficit.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the mobile-first layout and apply the same treatment to the downstream pages (opening an account, contact) so the layout does not change mid-journey.

recommendations.title: Have the pack message ready before the next annual search window
recommendations.finding: ING held 18.13% of Belgian brand search attention at rank 3 across Sep 2021–Sep 2026, down 2.49 points over the period, and its most recent annual slice is 16.79%. This is attention only, it says nothing about customers or conversion, and the data contains no cause for the movement.
recommendations.recommendation: Time any revision of the current-account pack copy to be live before the next annual window opens in September, so the message is in place for the period the series actually covers, and treat the link between the message and attention as a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.market_context: ING's share of brand-search attention is 18.13% (rank 3), down 2.49 points across Sep 2021–Sep 2026, with 16.79% in the latest annual slice; KBC holds the largest share at 21.3%.

recommendations.title: Study Crelan as the momentum benchmark
recommendations.finding: Crelan is the only benchmark flagged for momentum, up 3.84 points to 8.96% of attention with a relative slope of +16.4% per year over Sep 2021–Sep 2026, while ING is flagged as declining. The trajectory is a description of attention, not an effect of anything.
recommendations.recommendation: Compare Crelan's current-account page against ING's on structure, ordering of arguments and pack framing, and test one change from that comparison on the ING page rather than adopting the whole pattern.
recommendations.market_context: Crelan's share of Belgian brand-search attention rose 3.84 points to 8.96% (relative slope +16.4% per year) across Sep 2021–Sep 2026, against ING's decline of 2.49 points.

recommendations.title: Keep challenger conventions off the main pack page
recommendations.finding: The challenger segment accounts for 2.35% of brand search attention against 73.27% for the big four, and only Revolut is measurable (3.22% last share, up 2.63 points, relative slope +37.8% per year); the other challengers listed are low confidence and cannot be read. Whether challenger-style framing helps ING is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the main current-account page aimed at the big-four attention pool and, if a challenger-style proposition is worth testing, test it as a separate page variant rather than as the main framing.
recommendations.market_context: Challengers hold 2.35% of Belgian brand-search attention versus 73.27% for the big four, and only Revolut is measurable, at 3.22% last share and +2.63 points over Sep 2021–Sep 2026.

recommendations.title: Answer the transfer-limit question on the page
recommendations.finding: One of ING's 2 headlines in the last 90 days concerns banks limiting transfers to 5,000 € per day. ING's themes are only {other: 2}, so this is thin context, not evidence that visitors are asking it on the page, and the link between the theme and page behaviour is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a short FAQ block on the current-account and contact pages covering daily transfer limits and how to change them, then check on-page search terms before rolling the block out to other pages.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING appears in 2 headlines over the last 90 days, themes {other: 2}, one of them on banks limiting transfers to 5,000 € per day.

recommendations.title: Separate urgency language from security and access messaging
recommendations.finding: The recent news themes around ING's competitors are dominated by regulatory and data topics (Belfius: 30 headlines, 13 regulatory and 8 crisis-or-scandal; Revolut: 8 headlines, 5 crisis-or-scandal, on data-leak stories), while ING's own 2 headlines sit under {other: 2}. Amplifying urgency next to security copy is a framing risk, not a measured effect, and the link is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: On the current-account and account-opening pages, keep any countdown or scarcity element away from the security, data-protection and account-access sections, and write those sections in plain, factual language.
recommendations.reputation_context: Belfius: 30 headlines, themes {regulatory: 13, crisis_or_scandal: 8}; Revolut: 8 headlines, themes {crisis_or_scandal: 5, other: 3}; ING: 2 headlines, themes {other: 2}.

recommendations.title: Do not lean on unsupported innovation framing
recommendations.finding: ING appears in 2 headlines over the last 90 days, both under the theme 'other'; there is no coverage under innovation_digital, financial_results or regulatory. Any broad digital-leadership claim on the page would therefore sit outside what the press is currently covering, and that gap is a hypothesis to verify rather than a finding.
recommendations.recommendation: On the why-ING and current-account pages, replace broad innovation or digital-leadership framing with concrete, checkable statements about what the product does.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING: 2 headlines in the last 90 days, themes {other: 2}; no innovation_digital coverage, where BNP Paribas Fortis shows 1 headline under innovation_digital.
